results.evidence: Cache Col is mapped at 6,903 ft, and a climbing route description of the Cascade Pass area gives it as 6,900 ft. The approach prose (~6,900 ft) is right; the bivy entry's 6,400 is the outlier.

results.correct_value: Colonial Creek Campground trailhead on SR-20 just past milepost 130, ~1,200 ft
results.evidence: The Thunder Creek trail starts in Colonial Creek Campground just past SR-20 milepost 130; the trailhead sits at about 1,240 ft beside Diablo Lake (lake surface 1,201 ft). The waypoint's note described Rainy Pass (MP ~158) and its elev 4,875 is the Rainy Pass figure, contradicting the waypoint's own name, coordinates, directions and road.driveNote.

patches.find: Drive-to trailhead on SR-20 at Rainy Pass (milepost ~158); hike south on the Bridge Creek Trail/PCT ~9.5 mi (with ~2000 ft loss) to North Fork Group Camp, then leave trail cross-country toward the basin south of Storm King. Some parties instead approach from the south via the Lady of the Lake ferry to Stehekin + shuttle to High Bridge Camp, joining the same Bridge Creek/North Fork trail system. The current DB trailhead (Thunder Creek Trailhead / Colonial Creek Campground, ~48.6855,-121.0925) is a different, unconnected drainage well north of here and is very likely wrong.
patches.replace: Drive-to trailhead in Colonial Creek Campground on SR-20, just past milepost 130; the Thunder Creek Trail leaves from the south end of the campground near the amphitheater. The alternative southern start is by boat to Stehekin and shuttle to High Bridge, then up the Park Creek Trail.

results.correct_value: roughly 33 miles round trip for the Stehekin/Park Creek itinerary the days describe
results.evidence: The itinerary days describe the Stehekin approach: High Bridge to Park Creek is about 7.5-8 miles on foot, then ~2 miles up the Park Creek trail to Two Mile Camp, matching day 1's 9.5 mi; the day sum (33.5 mi) is consistent. The 40-45 mi figure in totalNote corresponds to the much longer Thunder Creek approach (waypoint distMi ~22 one way), not the itinerary shown.

results.fact: Rappel count and rope length for the descent
results.correct_value: Most parties downclimb; rappelling off the fixed slings is optional, and even with a 60 m rope some Class 3 downclimbing remains
results.evidence: One route description says a rappel off the east side returns you to the north-side ledge and that even with a 60 m rope some class 3 must be downclimbed; a detailed trip report downclimbed the route, noting slings near the summit show some parties rappel. One other party reported two rappels, so no count is stated in the new text; the '30 m is sufficient' claim is contradicted.

patches.fact: Rappel count and rope length for the descent
patches.find: parties typically make two short rappels off fixed slings (in-situ tat/webbing — inspect it and back it up before committing) to get back down through the ~15-ft crux crack and the exposed, Class 4 ledge just below it. Each rappel is short enough that a single 30m rope is sufficient, though many parties carry a 60m anyway for flexibility if linking up with nearby Goode or Buckner objectives on the same trip.
patches.replace: most parties downclimb the ~15-ft crux crack and the exposed Class 4 ledge just below it. Some instead rappel off the fixed slings (in-situ tat/webbing — inspect it and back it up before committing) back to the ledge on the north side; even with a 60 m rope, expect to downclimb some Class 3 terrain.

patches.fact: Descent line below the summit (Black Tooth Notch / southwest couloir belong to Goode)

results.fact: Where the climbers' path leaves the maintained trail (Park Creek Pass traverse vs the ~4,100 ft washout on the Park Creek trail)
results.evidence: approach, the rib-camp waypoint directions and approach_variants say to leave the trail AT Park Creek Pass and traverse west/southwest about a mile to the cirque, while itinerary day 2 (and the approach variant's Stehekin sentence) leave the Park Creek trail at a large washout near 4,100 ft and climb to a 7,400 ft basin. A route description has Thunder Creek parties cross the pass and descend into Park Creek, and a trip report descended from the basin to the Park Creek trail, which favours the low washout start; the row's own coordinates also place Storm King east of the pass, not west. Rewriting the whole Thunder Creek narrative and several waypoint directions was not attempted without a clearer second description of the high traverse.

results.correct_value: Emergency: 911 or Skagit County Sheriff dispatch (360) 336-9450; Wilderness Information Center (360) 854-7245
results.evidence: The park's contact page lists Visitor Information (360) 854-7200 and the Wilderness Information Center (360) 854-7245, and its climbing-safety page says to call 911 or Skagit County Sheriff's Office dispatch (360) 336-9450. The (360) 873-4500 dispatch number in comms appears nowhere; 854-7200 is the general visitor line, not the WIC. The 873-4590 ext. 37 and 856-5700 ext. 515 figures in emergency.notes are corroborated only by one dated compilation and are left untouched; the rangerStation 'park main line 856-5700' is replaced with the WIC number the park publishes.

patches.find: Park dispatch can be reached at (360) 873-4500 ext. 37 in emergency situations, though response times may be slow. The Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount at (360) 854-7200 can provide emergency coordination.

results.evidence: gain_ft 3920 is exactly the net rise from the 3,600 ft trailhead to the 7,520 ft summit, the range a trip report gives (9.3 mi round trip, 3,600-7,520 ft); loss_ft, itinerary gainFt/lossFt and totalNote say ~5,410, which would include the height lost dropping from the ridge to the glacier and bumps on the ridge. results.fact: Number and length of the summit rappel
results.evidence: The only detailed report found downclimbed several spots and then made two 30 m rappels (rope plus tagline) from stations on the east ridge, which is the basis of the rappels field; it noted a rappel station on the ridge. descent/pitch_detail/itinerary describe one short single-rope rappel off the summit tower, and descent_text says downclimb.
